claims.text: The CDC study found a possible higher risk of thrombotic events, including stroke, for up to a year after COVID-19.
claims.quote: In conclusion, this study identified a possible elevated risk for thrombotic events, including stroke, up to a year after COVID-19, especially among patients hospitalized with COVID-19. This risk appears to remain higher for patients with COVID-19 than for those with ARI.

claims.text: The unadjusted risk for ischemic stroke was higher after COVID-19 than after other acute respiratory infections in every interval from 31 to 365 days.
claims.quote: The unadjusted risk for ischemic stroke was higher among patients with COVID-19 compared with patients with ARI in every time interval and among both hospitalized and nonhospitalized patients (hospitalized patient incidence ratio 1.13 for 31–90 days, 1.26 for 91–180 days, 1.12 for 181–365 days; nonhospitalized patient incidence ratio 1.65 for 31–90 days, 1.68 for 91–180 days, 1.77 for 181–365 days) (p<0.0001).
